title: New big rig safety tech could save your life
summary: Daimler Truck's Oregon demos show how a Freightliner Cascadia's automatic emergency braking responds when dummy cars suddenly cross a moving truck's path.
story: Daimler Truck's advanced safety systems use radar and cameras to monitor surrounding vehicles and help prevent dangerous collisions. (Joe Raedle/Newsmakers via Getty Images)

Ever find yourself driving next to a massive 18-wheeler and wondering if the driver can actually see your car? It's a reasonable concern. Big rigs have enormous blind spots, and stopping one takes a lot more time and distance than stopping your car. Now, new big rig safety tech from Daimler Truck could help prevent some of the most dangerous crashes on our roads.

The company behind Freightliner is upgrading its trucks with technology that can recognize potential collisions and automatically hit the brakes. We're talking about situations where another driver suddenly cuts across a truck's path or a pedestrian gets dangerously close during a turn. And demonstrations at Daimler's Oregon proving grounds offer a revealing look at what happens when this technology faces situations that could turn deadly on public roads.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
100 KODIAK DRIVERLESS TRUCKS ARE HEADED FOR PUBLIC ROADS
What happens when a car suddenly cuts in front of a big rig?

At Daimler Truck's testing facility in Oregon, engineers recreated situations that could easily turn deadly on a public road. They used dummy cars mounted on remote-controlled platforms to simulate vehicles suddenly crossing in front of a moving Freightliner Cascadia. In one demonstration, the truck successfully avoided a collision. In another, it clipped the dummy car after braking. That second test may sound like a failure, but consider what could have happened if the truck had continued at full speed. Slowing down before impact can make an enormous difference when a passenger car comes face-to-face with a fully loaded truck.

The demonstrations generally took place at speeds between 40 and 55 mph. Daimler said the truck's trailer carried approximately 30,000 pounds during the tests. That's a lot of weight pushing forward when the brakes suddenly engage. And here's what caught my attention. The technology was designed to recognize these developing dangers and respond even when the driver had little time to react. That's especially important because a few seconds can determine how serious a collision becomes.
How big rig safety tech spots trouble before a crash

The technology comes from Detroit Assurance, Daimler Truck North America's collection of advanced driver assistance systems. At the center is Active Brake Assist 6, also known as ABA6. It uses five radar sensors and a camera to monitor what's happening around the truck. Together, they provide approximately 270 degrees of coverage, including areas alongside a standard 53-foot trailer.

Think of it as another set of electronic eyes helping the driver keep track of nearby traffic. The system can identify certain vehicles that have stopped unexpectedly, including cars sitting at unusual angles after an accident. For example, a truck approaching a crash scene might encounter a disabled vehicle partly blocking the roadway. Active Brake Assist 6 is designed to recognize these situations and warn the driver. If necessary, it can also apply the brakes.

The technology can recognize pedestrians and cyclists in certain scenarios, too. That's particularly useful when a large truck travels through busy areas where people may be difficult to see from the cab. And Daimler is now expanding those capabilities to address another dangerous situation.
WHAT HAPPENS IF THE WAYMO COMPUTER FAILS?
Freightliner’s latest safety systems use radar and cameras to monitor traffic around big rigs and respond when a collision threat develops. (Stock Photos)
New Freightliner safety systems can brake at intersections

Intersections can be especially challenging for truck drivers. They have to maneuver a massive vehicle while watching traffic that may approach from several directions. All it takes is one person making an unexpected move. That's where a new feature called Cross Traffic Assist comes in. The system uses radar to detect vehicles crossing the truck's path at intersections. If it recognizes a potential collision, it can alert the driver with audible and visual warnings. When the danger becomes more serious, it can also apply partial or full braking. Now, think about what that could mean if someone accidentally pulls out in front of an approaching truck. The system may give the driver extra time to respond or help reduce the force of a collision.

Another improvement involves Active Side Guard Assist 2. The enhanced system adds protection when the truck makes a left turn across oncoming traffic. With the left turn signal activated, it can recognize certain approaching vehicles and warn the driver. If necessary, it can also apply the brakes. The new left-turn protection builds on existing safety technology that monitors the passenger-side blind spot during right turns. That system can detect pedestrians and cyclists and apply braking when necessary.

These improvements are scheduled to become standard on Freightliner Cascadias built beginning in 2027, with production planned for January. Active Brake Assist 6 itself is already standard on the fifth-generation Cascadia. According to Daimler Truck North America, the goal is to give professional drivers additional support when visibility or reaction time becomes limited.
What if a truck driver suddenly stops responding?

There's another feature that deserves attention because it addresses a frightening possibility. What happens if someone behind the wheel of a big rig suddenly becomes unresponsive? Freightliner's optional Active Lane Assist 2 can help keep the truck centered in its lane and correct unintended drifting. It can also provide steering assistance during certain challenging driving conditions, such as strong crosswinds.

But the feature I find particularly interesting is called Attentive Driver Protection. When the lane-keeping system is active, Attentive Driver Protection monitors whether the driver continues responding. If the driver fails to respond to escalating warnings, the technology can slow the truck to a stop while helping keep it centered in its lane. It can also activate the hazard lights to warn surrounding traffic.

Consider the potential consequences of a driver becoming unresponsive while operating a massive truck on a busy highway. Having an additional safety system that can help bring the vehicle to a controlled stop could make a significant difference. However, the feature doesn't diagnose medical emergencies or determine why a driver has stopped responding. It reacts to a lack of driver response under specific conditions. And like the other safety systems, it still depends on factors such as road conditions and sensor performance.
HUMANLESS BIG RIG COMPLETES FIRST US FREIGHT RUN
Freightliner’s Attentive Driver Protection can slow a truck to a stop if the driver stops responding to escalating warnings. (Noah Berger, File/AP Photo)
What this means to you

You may never drive a Freightliner, but chances are you share the road with big rigs regularly. And that's why these improvements should interest you. If a truck can recognize a dangerous situation and begin braking before the driver has time to react, the people in nearby vehicles could have a better chance of avoiding serious injuries. Even reducing the speed of an unavoidable collision could make a significant difference.

But don't assume every truck you encounter has these features. Many older trucks won't have the newest technology, and even equipped vehicles have limitations. Sensors can struggle in poor weather or when visibility becomes limited. Automatic braking also cannot guarantee that every collision will be avoided.

So, continue giving big rigs plenty of room. Avoid lingering beside a truck where the driver might have trouble seeing you. And when passing, make sure there's sufficient space before moving back into its lane. Remember that even the smartest technology cannot change the physics of a massive truck traveling at highway speed. The safest approach is to stay alert and avoid putting yourself in a situation where a truck driver has to make a sudden move.
Kurt's key takeaways

Here's what I find encouraging about Daimler's latest safety technology. It recognizes something we all know about driving. People make mistakes. Someone misjudges an intersection or pulls out without realizing how quickly a truck is approaching. Those split-second decisions can have terrible consequences, especially when a massive vehicle has little room to stop. The demonstrations in Oregon showed why this technology has potential. In one scenario, the truck avoided a collision. In another, contact still occurred, but the braking reduced the impact. That second result is an important reminder that a safety system can still provide protection even when it cannot prevent every accident. I also think we're seeing an interesting shift in how truck manufacturers approach safety. There's been plenty of attention on trucks that can drive themselves. Yet here we have technology designed to help professional drivers do their jobs more safely. And when you consider how many trucks share our highways, even modest improvements in collision prevention could have an enormous impact. Of course, controlled demonstrations are one thing. Everyday traffic brings unexpected challenges that are much harder to predict. I'll be interested to see how these systems perform as more equipped trucks reach the road. If the technology can prevent serious crashes, that's something we can all appreciate.

Would you feel safer knowing an 18-wheeler could automatically brake to avoid hitting your car, or would you still be nervous driving alongside a massive truck that relies on software to react? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

title: Masked dirt bike riders swarm SUV in brazen NYC street attack, sparking police crackdown
summary: Video captures masked dirt bike riders swarming and attacking an SUV on a busy Staten Island street as the NYPD warns that arrests are near.
story: A group of masked dirt bike riders was caught on video kicking and punching a vehicle at a Staten Island intersection before chasing the driver down the road.

New York City officials are warning a group of masked dirt bike riders that arrests could be imminent after video captured a chaotic confrontation in which several riders surrounded and attacked a vehicle on a busy Staten Island street.
The crackdown follows a Wednesday incident on Richmond Avenue in Staten Island's Bulls Head neighborhood, where video showed several masked riders swarming a white SUV stopped at a traffic light.

In the video obtained by Fox News Digital, several individuals appeared to kick and strike the vehicle, while another appeared to throw an object at it. As the driver attempted to leave, the SUV appeared to run over a dirt bike that had been positioned in front of the vehicle.
WATCH: E-BIKE TEEN TAKEOVER SWARMS DOWNTOWN CITY STREETS BLOCKING TRAFFIC, LEADING TO CHARGES

A group of masked dirt bike riders surrounded a white SUV on Richmond Avenue in Staten Island, where several individuals appeared to kick and strike the vehicle. (Facebook/Staten Island Bad Parking & Driving)
During a news conference Thursday, NYPD Assistant Chief John Buttacavoli warned those involved that police were gathering intelligence and working to identify the suspects.
"We know who you are, and you will be getting a knock on your door very soon," Buttacavoli said, emphasizing that the behavior had escalated from a quality-of-life concern into criminal activity.
"It stops here. We're taking action," he added.
Staten Island District Attorney Michael McMahon also condemned the riders, accusing them of intimidating motorists and putting innocent people at risk.
VIDEO SHOWS BRIDGE TURN INTO BURNOUT BONANZA IN STUNT-HAPPY TAKEOVER – POLICE SWOOP IN TO CUFF ROAD REBELS

"Like a plague of locusts, they descend upon drivers who are just going about their business here on Staten Island," McMahon said. "They're jackals, they're teenage terrorists, and it's not going to be tolerated here in our borough."
McMahon called the behavior "simply outrageous," adding that no one had been seriously injured, based on the information available to officials.
Wednesday's incident was part of a broader pattern of dangerous behavior involving motorized bikes, according to Staten Island Borough President Vito Fossella.
Fossella described the riders as a "bunch of punks who are literally terrorizing drivers" as motorists went about their daily routines.
"Enough. This game is over," Fossella said.
The borough president also warned parents that their children were putting innocent motorists at risk.
CITIES FEARING HALLOWEEN MAYHEM PUT TEENS ON NOTICE, ANNOUNCE CURFEWS AND CRACKDOWNS AFTER VIOLENT TAKEOVERS

NYPD Assistant Chief John Buttacavoli warned that police were working to identify those involved in an incident where masked dirt bike riders swarmed a vehicle on Staten Island. (Staten Island District Attorney's Office)
"Your kid is terrorizing innocent people when they're just going about their business. It's wrong, and it needs to stop," Fossella said.

McMahon warned that parents could face legal or financial consequences if their children use illegal motorized vehicles to intimidate or injure others, including potential civil liability if someone is hurt.
"Parents also must take responsibility for their children," McMahon's office said in a separate statement.

Police have assembled a task force to address the problem and will continue confiscating illegally operated motorized bikes, according to Buttacavoli. He said officers had already identified several individuals and seized numerous bikes this year.
GRINNING SUSPECT CUFFED AFTER ALLEGED FIERY STREET TAKEOVER, DRAG RACE CAUGHT ON CAMERA

Staten Island Borough President Vito Fossella, District Attorney Michael McMahon and NYPD Assistant Chief John Buttacavoli addressed a confrontation involving masked dirt bike riders and an SUV during a news conference. (Staten Island District Attorney's Office)
The NYPD also reminded residents that certain motorized vehicles must be registered, insured and operated by licensed drivers.

State Assemblyman Mike Reilly, R-Staten Island, said he plans to introduce legislation in January that would hold parents financially responsible for minors caught recklessly operating certain motorized vehicles, according to the New York Post.
The proposal would impose fines ranging from $250 to $1,500, the paper reported.

The incident remains under investigation, and no arrests have been announced.

title: At least 100 people pulled from Mississippi River after New Orleans ship crash as lengthy salvage effort looms
summary: Officials say roughly 100 people were pulled from the Mississippi River after the Atlantic Asphalt tanker struck the docked American Heritage cruise ship in New Orleans on Friday.
story: Mayor Helena Moreno says Saturday that the boat's injured captain was the last to leave the vessel after Friday's crash, which could take weeks to remove from the Mississippi River.

Roughly 100 people were pulled from the Mississippi River after a tanker struck a docked cruise ship in New Orleans on Friday, officials revealed Saturday, as the U.S. Coast Guard prepares for a potentially weeks-long operation to remove the capsized vessel.
New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno said 191 passengers and crew members were aboard the American Heritage when the Atlantic Asphalt tanker struck the vessel near the Port of New Orleans.
Everyone survived, though eight people remained hospitalized Saturday, including two in serious condition. The other six patients were stable, officials said.

Coast Guard Capt. Melanie Burnham said crews were preparing to remove 16,000 gallons of fuel from the American Heritage before salvage operations begin. Divers were expected to assess the vessel, while pollution response teams monitored the river for potential leaks.
NEW ORLEANS BOAT CRASH CALLED ‘MIRACLE ON THE MISSISSIPPI’ AS EVERYONE IS ACCOUNTED FOR, OFFICIALS SAY
Tugboats surround the Atlantic Asphalt tanker in New Orleans following its collision with the docked American Heritage river cruiser on Nov. 13, 2026. (Kat Ramirez for Fox News Digital)
Burnham said crews had not observed any product in the river requiring removal but warned that hazardous materials could potentially escape during the operation.
"As the mayor said, we're talking weeks, we're not talking days, we're talking weeks. So we're going to do this safely, and we're going to make sure that it's done right," Burnham said.
Moreno also revealed that the American Heritage's captain was injured but remained aboard until passengers and crew were accounted for, becoming the last person to leave the vessel.
"Every moment of the critical time [Friday], he did not want to leave his ship," Moreno said.
TWO DEAD, INCLUDING INFANT, AFTER BOAT CAPSIZES IN NEW YORK HARBOR; 12 RESCUED
Port of New Orleans collision map (Fox News)
The captain initially refused medical treatment until he knew where everyone was, according to the mayor.
Port of New Orleans Harbor Police Chief Melanie Montro said responders evacuated more than 80 people before the vessel overturned, while roughly 100 people ended up in the river.
Montro said she estimated the American Heritage capsized within 30 to 45 minutes of the collision, though the exact timeline remains under investigation.
Officials credited life jackets and the rapid response of emergency crews and nearby vessels with preventing fatalities.
Investigators are examining a possible steering issue involving the tanker, though the exact cause of the collision remains unknown.
"I can say though I do not have any indication that this is terrorism related in any way, shape or form, but again, the investigators will continue to keep working through that," Burnham said.
11-NIGHT CARIBBEAN CRUISE ABRUPTLY CANCELED AFTER COAST GUARD DETAINS SHIP

The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) confirmed Saturday that investigators recovered the Atlantic Asphalt's voyage data recorder, which captures information including the vessel's speed, course and audio from its bridge.

NTSB board member John DeLeeuw said during a news conference Saturday that investigators will also examine the tanker's maintenance records and mechanical history as they work to determine what caused the collision.
He cautioned that the agency remains in the early stages of gathering evidence and has not reached any conclusions.
DeLeeuw and a team of NTSB investigators began arriving Saturday after travel disruptions delayed its response.
NTSB board member John DeLeeuw addresses questions from media Saturday in New Orleans after a tanker crash with a riverboat cruise ship on the Mississippi River. (WVUE)
DeLeeuw said 16 investigators were on scene and preparing to interview crew members and others involved.
The agency said it expects to release a preliminary report in about 30 days, with a final report identifying probable causes and potential safety recommendations expected in 18 to 24 months.
The collision occurred around 12:30 p.m. local time Friday, when the tanker struck the American Heritage, which had been docked for approximately two hours.
The vessel began taking on water before capsizing.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The Atlantic Asphalt has since been moved from the collision site, while the Coast Guard has partially reopened the river to two-way traffic. A 500-foot safety zone remains in place around the wreck.
American Cruise Lines, which operates American Heritage, is coordinating with local officials to assist displaced passengers as the investigation and recovery efforts continue.
Brittany Miller is a Fox News Digital breaking news writer and former Independent reporter who graduated from Syracuse University in 2023.

title: MICHAEL RUIZ: Montauk bikini designer's $50M yacht death lawsuit frozen as owner asks judge for exoneration
summary: Christopher Durnan invoked maritime law to cap liability after Martha Nolan-O'Slatarra was found dead on a New York yacht at Montauk Yacht Club.
story: Speaking with Fox News Digital, Attorney Michael Bowe discusses the family's $50 million wrongful death suit and reveals EMTs found blood on NYC fashion designer Martha Nolan-O’Slatarra aboard a Montauk yacht.

The family of an Irish bikini designer found dead aboard a luxe yacht at a high-end New York marina is treading water after a federal judge put their state-level wrongful death lawsuit on hold while the boat's owner seeks exoneration or liability limited to less than 1% of their $50 million demand under maritime law.
Martha Nolan-O'Slatarra was a 33-year-old Irish expat and New York fashion designer whom police found dead on a 54-foot Sea Ray named "Ripple" at the Montauk Yacht Club in August 2025.

The 61-year-old yacht owner Christopher Durnan, a multimillionaire insurance mogul and investor in the woman's summerwear business, has now turned to federal maritime law in a bid to avoid liability altogether or cap his potential exposure at $476,942, which his attorneys said is the vessel's appraised value.
FAMILY OF BIKINI DESIGNER IN MONTAUK YACHT DEATH FILES $50M LAWSUIT ALLEGING ASSAULT
"This is a typical delay tactic that is rarely successful and will not be here," said Michael Bowe, a New York attorney representing Nolan-O'Slatarra's family.
"Mr. Durnan will soon have to answer to the complaint we are prepared to file and then to sit for his deposition."
Martha Nolan, 33, owned a swimwear company based in Manhattan, N.Y. Her brand featured high-end bikinis. (Facebook/Martha Nolan)
James Mercante, an attorney for Durnan who specializes in maritime law, declined to comment.

Filings like Durnan's are common, according to David Cattie, an attorney based in the U.S. Virgin Islands and another expert on federal maritime law. He said vessel owners have "vastly more protection" at sea than on land, if the facts of the case meet federal criteria.
"But if they are claiming, and can prove, direct involvement or knowledge by the owner, those protections evaporate," he told Fox News Digital.

"In short, he is asking the court to invoke admiralty’s jurisdiction to stop the state court claims," he said. "He is also asking the court for exoneration, [the] owner has no liability at all, or limitation, which caps liability and exposure to the value of the vessel post incident."
Martha Nolan-O'Slatarra, a 33-year-old Irish expat and New York fashion designer, was found dead at the Montauk Yacht Club in August 2025. (GoFundMe)

The federal court battle will focus in part on what's known as "privity," he said, whether the circumstances that allegedly caused or contributed to Nolan-O'Slatarra's death involved something Durnan personally knew about or was responsible for.
GABBY PETITO COURT BATTLE COULD DECIDE WHETHER CHARLIE KIRK FAMILY CAN PREVAIL IN UTAH WRONGFUL DEATH LAWSUIT
"If the owner was involved in or knew of the defect that caused the harm, he cannot limit his liability to the value of the vessel," he said.

Christopher Durnan holding a guitar painted in a similar design to the Grateful Dead band's logo in a split image next to a shot of the Ripple, a 54-foot Sea Ray Yacht where summerwear fashion designer Martha Nolan was found dead. (Left: Doug Kuntz, Right: Christopher Durnan/LinkedIn)
Even though the boat was docked in the marina at the time, it was still legally in what's considered a "navigable waterway," Cattie added.

"If the harm transpired on the vessel, it would be subject to Admiralty jurisdiction," Cattie told Fox News Digital. "If it happened on the dock and the deceased was moved to the vessel, it would probably not."
WOMAN FOUND DEAD ON YACHT SPARKS SCRUTINY OF MONTAUK’S PARTY SCENE AND RISING WEALTH
Durnan has denied wrongdoing and has not been charged with a crime, and his attorneys have denied any fault or neglect on his part.

According to his federal court filing, Nolan-O'Slatarra was a guest aboard the Ripple on Aug. 4, 2025. Around midnight on Aug. 5, she was unconscious and unresponsive, and Durnan attempted to render aid, according to the filing. Durnan's lawyers wrote that he sought help from people aboard other vessels at the marina. One of them called 911, and another performed CPR on Nolan-O'Slatarra.

What appears to be a white powdery substance is seen here in photos of the boat where Suffolk County police have identified the woman found dead on the boat named "Ripple," which is docked at the Montauk Yacht Club, as Martha Nolan O'Slattara, a 33-year-old and founder of East x East from Manhattan. (hoo-me.com/MediaPunch /IPX via AP)

"If any fault caused or contributed to the claims for loss, damage and/or fatality, which is denied, such fault, neglect, or want of care was occasioned and occurred without the Petitioner’s privity or knowledge," Durnan's lawyers wrote. "The Petitioner acted reasonably under the circumstances."

Although the wrongful death lawsuit was filed in August, Durnan had not been served with it until Oct. 1, according to court filings. He had not authorized his attorney to accept service on his behalf and could not be found at his waterfront home on New York's Long Island; another one in nearby Garden City, where they saw a Lamborghini registered to his name; or a third in Windham, New York, about 150 miles from New York City, according to Bowe, who represents the designer's estate.
Nolan-O'Slatarra's family faced a 120-day deadline to serve the lawsuit.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X
Law enforcement officers gather near luxury yachts at the Montauk Yacht Club marina as part of an active investigation into the death of 33-year-old Martha Nolan. (WNYW)

A process server eventually found Durnan at a fourth property, his waterfront vacation home in Lantana, Florida, where they found a Rolls-Royce parked outside, according to court records. After a days-long stakeout involving multiple process servers and private investigators, Durnan was finally served, allegedly telling one he "was surprised it took you so long."
The next day, Durnan turned to a federal judge with his petition to avoid or limit potential liability, court records show.

"When we have trouble serving someone, it's a red flag that something fishy is going on," said Randolph Rice, a Maryland-based attorney and legal analyst. "Ultimately, this maritime maneuver may give the defense a legal lifeline, but it's far from clear whether the argument will float with the federal court."

Durnan is invoking the same federal maritime law used by the owner of the cargo ship that struck Baltimore's Francis Scott Key Bridge in 2024 in an effort to limit its liability for the disaster, Rice said.
The boat named Ripple, docked at The Star Island Marina in Montauk early on Aug. 5, 2025. (Doug Kuntz)

On Oct. 27, U.S. Magistrate Judge Gabriel W. Gorenstein approved Durnan's request to put up the appraised value of the boat as substitute collateral and ordered that related lawsuits "hereby are restrained, stayed and enjoined until the hearing and determination of this action."
He also gave Nolan-O'Slatarra's family a chance to dispute Durnan's request. The judge set a Jan. 25, 2027, deadline for potential claimants to enter the federal case and challenge Durnan's bid.

Town of East Hampton police arrived at the Montauk Yacht Club around midnight on Aug. 5, 2025, in response to a report of an unconscious woman aboard Durnan's boat. It was Nolan-O'Slatarra, who was pronounced dead.
A law enforcement official, wearing disposable blue cleaning gloves, is seen investigating the yacht where 33-year-old Martha Nolan was found Aug. 5, 2025. (Doug Kuntz)

According to Suffolk County police, forensic pathologists found no signs of violence, but her final cause of death was pending additional investigation.

However, in a wrongful death lawsuit filed earlier this year, her family alleged Durnan assaulted Nolan-O'Slatarra or otherwise engaged in grossly negligent, reckless and wanton conduct that caused her injuries and death.

"The EMTs, when they arrived, found blood in her mouth, on her chest, on her head, and they believe behind her, behind her head," Bowe told Fox News Digital in August.

title: Sexual predator deported to Mexico hauled back to US for assault and murder of American mom
summary: Miguel Angel Urbano-Vazquez was deported to Mexico after Sharon Van Gilder's 2002 murder but was later extradited and convicted decades later.
story: Brenda Doty, the cousin of murder victim Sharon Van Gilder, spoke with Fox News Digital about her family’s nearly 25-year fight for justice and her fears that the convicted serial rapist may have more victims.
A serial rapist from Mexico who murdered an American woman more than two decades ago and terrorized other women in the United States has finally been brought to justice.

Miguel Angel Urbano-Vazquez, who was previously deported to Mexico before being extradited back to the U.S., was found guilty earlier this month of aggravated first-degree murder in the March 2002 rape and strangulation of 39-year-old Sharon Van Gilder in Washington state.
Her body was discovered along a rural road in Pierce County, Washington.
Van Gilder's cousin, Brenda Doty, told Fox News Digital the fact that her killer was finally convicted nearly 25 years later is an overwhelming relief.
The family of a mother of two murdered in 2002 is finally seeing justice, but her cousin fears the killer's violent past holds even more dark secrets. (Pierce County Sheriff's Office)
YOGURT SHOP MURDERS FUEL FAMILY QUESTIONS ABOUT ACCOMPLICE AS RAGE LINGERS OVER WRONGFULLY ACCUSED
"I'd wake up in the middle of the night thinking about it," Doty said. "She didn't deserve that."
Van Gilder, a mother of two, was close with her family.
"We just had so much fun together, riding ponies and horses and playing in the barn," Doty said.
Sharon Van Gilder, 39, was murdered by convicted killer and serial rapist Miguel Urbano-Vazquez, 50. (Pierce County Prosecutor's Office)
Doty remembers her cousin not just as a wonderful friend, but as a hero who decades ago saved her own daughter from drowning in a lake during a family outing.
"[Sharon] jumped into the water, swam over there, dove underneath and pulled her up. She saved my daughter's life," Doty said.
"My daughter was 8 years old, and she's 40 now," she said.
More than two decades after terrorizing women and killing a mother of two, a serial rapist has finally been brought to justice. (Pierce County Sheriff's Office)
Van Gilder was last seen leaving a bar in Tacoma with the killer and another man in March 2002, the Pierce County Sheriff's Office said.
KILLER UNDONE BY DECADES-OLD THREADS — GLOVE, TOWEL AND SHIRT STITCH TOGETHER COLD CASE JUSTICE
Hours later, her naked and badly beaten body was discovered on the side of a road in Spanaway, southeast of Tacoma. Investigators determined she had been strangled.

More than two decades after terrorizing women and killing a mother of two, a serial rapist has finally been brought to justice. (Pierce County Sheriff's Office)
Prosecutors said Van Gilder was the first victim in a series of violent sexual assaults between March and October 2002.
PATEL TOUTS FBI DNA BREAKTHROUGH HE SAYS BUSTED ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT IN DECADE-LONG SERIAL RAPE CASE
Urbano-Vazquez was deported to Mexico sometime after Van Gilder's killing, the FBI Seattle said.
Knowing his history, Doty suspects the trail of violence is even longer.
"I'm sure [from the time] when he was in Mexico, there are more [victims]," she said.
KILLER’S CHEWING GUM BLOWS OPEN 40-YEAR-OLD MURDERS, DETECTIVE WARNS THERE MAY BE MORE VICTIMS
"He's such a violent, violent person."

The Pierce County Prosecutor's Office said, "In 2012, DNA tests linked the 2002 rape and murder of Sharon Van Gilder to three other nearby rapes. Suspect Miguel Urbano-Vazquez was captured abroad in 2023 and extradited in 2025, when a DNA sample could be taken and compared to the 2002 samples."

A serial rapist who murdered a mother of two in 2002 was convicted after being deported to Mexico and later extradited back to the United States. (Pierce County Sheriff's Office)

title: NYC woman allegedly struck by LGBTQ+ activist after questioning trans youth treatments: 'Never have answers'
summary: LGBTQ+ activist Jay Walker allegedly elbowed a counter-protester outside Mount Sinai Hospital in New York City as she questioned his support for youth transgender procedures.
story: A New York City woman, Christiane Torello, says she was elbowed in the chest by queer activist Jay Walker during a rally outside Mount Sinai Hospital in Manhattan as she was questioning his support for transgender treatment for minors.

A woman says she was assaulted by a prominent LGBTQ+ activist at a recent New York City protest as she was questioning his push for transgender medical procedures for children, according to video of the incident provided by the alleged victim.

Christiane Torello was a counter-protester at the rally outside Mount Sinai Hospital in Manhattan on Nov. 5 when she was allegedly elbowed in the chest by Jay Walker, the president of Gays Against Guns who also served as a 2026 NYC Pride grand marshal.

Walker was part of a group rallying against the hospital's decision in September to end transgender treatments for minors to resolve a Department of Justice investigation into youth gender transition procedures.
MAJOR BLUE STATE HOSPITAL PULLS PLUG ON CONTROVERSIAL CHILD TRANSGENDER TREATMENTS AFTER DOJ INTERVENTION
"The hospital is no longer providing any type of gender-affirming care for minors, including surgeries, puberty blockers and hormones," Torello told Fox News Digital.

"There’s always a group of individuals who go to these protests to show their discomfort and displeasure with the hospital stopping these procedures because they want the children to transition. I usually go there in opposition to them. I support the hospital’s decision to stop providing that care. I always go by myself and ask questions."
A man identified as Jay Walker was part of a group rallying against Mount Sinai Hospital's decision in September to end transgender treatments for minors. (Erik McGregor/LightRocket via Getty Images)

In the video she captured of the incident, Torello asked Walker why he wanted to "have penises in the locker room" as he was yelling and walking away from her on a sidewalk. Walker then stopped, wound his elbow up and allegedly struck her in the chest before repeatedly shouting, "Get away from me."
She said demonstrators often attempt to obstruct her path and shove their signs in her face, but this incident was more violent than most of the rallies she has been to.

"I'm usually followed around the protest by two or three people. They block me and put signs in my face, which is fine because they’re allowed to do that. But this time, it became particularly violent," Torello said.

"When I asked the organizer of the protest, Jay Walker, what size dongs he’d like in the girls’ locker room, he didn’t have an answer. They never have answers to those questions. They don’t like to talk about it," she continued.
Torello said Walker was shouting slurs at her as he was walking away from the protest, and she followed him to question him more about what he was saying.
She then accused Walker of hitting her in the chest with his elbow, adding that she thinks he intended to strike her in the face but had "pretty bad aim."

"As we were walking, he stopped in front of me, wound up his elbow and blasted me in the chest," she said. "He’s about 6-5, and I’m 5-5, so I’m pretty sure he intended to hit me in the face but had pretty bad aim and hit me in the chest."
After the alleged assault, Torello continued following Walker down the street.
UTAH STUDENT CITED AFTER PHYSICAL ALTERCATION WITH COLLEGE REPUBLICAN CAUGHT ON CAMERA
Christiane Torello accused Jay Walker of hitting her in the chest with his elbow as he was leaving the protest. (Erik McGregor/LightRocket via Getty Images)
The video shows both Torello and Walker yelling and cursing at one another as they were walking.

Walker was heard calling her "psychotic," "scumbag," a "garbage person" and a "stalker," while she accused him of being a "woman abuser." At one point, he allegedly lunged at Torello, and she dared him to "do it again," saying she would post the video on social media.
"I'm so glad I got it on camera," she shouted at Walker.
Torello told Fox News Digital she reported the incident to the New York City Police Department, but she is not confident any charges will be filed.
"I want to press charges because I feel like New York doesn’t do anything when it comes to a lot of violence," she said.

"But this is a different type of violence. I have a First Amendment right to be there and peacefully protest. I wasn’t hitting anybody. Do I ask questions that may be annoying or triggering? Sure. But that’s the extent of what I do. That doesn’t warrant me getting hit, elbowed or punched."
Mount Sinai Hospital in New York City moved to end transgender treatments for minors in September to resolve a Department of Justice investigation. (Bryan Bedder/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"This is actually the second time a man has put his hands on me at a protest," she continued.

"The first happened about a month and a half ago. There were two NYPD detectives in front of that other protester who watched me get hit, and they didn’t even talk to me. I asked them if they could direct me somewhere, and they wouldn’t say one word to me. I had to figure it out on my own. I filed a report, and nothing happened to that man either."
It is unclear if police plan to make any arrests in the alleged assault.
The NYPD and Walker's group, Gays Against Guns NY, did not respond to Fox News Digital's multiple requests for comment.
"I just really hope this brings some awareness and puts pressure on the NYPD to do something, because they don’t do anything at all," Torello said.

title: New Orleans boat crash called ‘miracle on the Mississippi’ as everyone is accounted for, officials say
summary: Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry called it "a literal miracle on the Mississippi" after a tanker capsized the American Heritage cruiser in New Orleans.
story: Travelers aboard the American Heritage share their experiences after a tanker struck the docked river cruiser in New Orleans, causing it to capsize and triggering a rescue operation. Credit: Kat Ramirez for Fox News Digital

Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry called it "a literal miracle on the Mississippi" Friday after officials said everyone was accounted for following a tanker collision that capsized a docked New Orleans river cruiser and sent 32 passengers to hospitals.
"This is a miracle," Landry said at a news conference. "The Mississippi River is not some quiet pond, right? I mean, there were challenges out there."
Mayor Helena Moreno said none of the hospitalized passengers had critical injuries. Two Harbor Police officers were also hospitalized and were in good condition, officials said.
CRUISE PASSENGER HAILED AS HERO AFTER JUMPING INTO WATER TO SAVE 84-YEAR-OLD MAN

The Atlantic Asphalt tanker and American Heritage river cruiser after a collision on the Mississippi River in New Orleans Nov. 13, 2026. The cruiser was docked with about 129 passengers, plus crew members, aboard, port officials said. (Facebook/Tarzan Duran)
"We have zero people unaccounted for, which is a miracle," Moreno said, crediting local, state and federal responders who jumped into the water to help.
Coast Guard Capt. Melanie Burnham confirmed the search and rescue operation had ended.
"We got everybody," Landry added.
TEEN BOATER FOUND CLINGING TO CAPSIZED VESSEL AFTER 3 GO MISSING; 2 BODIES RECOVERED
Tugboats surround the Atlantic Asphalt tanker in New Orleans following its collision with the docked American Heritage river cruiser on Nov. 13, 2026. (Kat Ramirez for Fox News Digital)

Officials said the tanker lost control before striking the American Heritage. Passengers were evacuating when the cruiser began taking on water and capsized, leaving some people in the river and others on a portion of the vessel still above water.

Harbor Police responded first, firefighters lowered ladders over the dock and nearby vessels helped pull people from the water. New Orleans Police Superintendent Anne Kirkpatrick said a police drone already airborne for an unrelated theft call was redirected to the crash within moments.
Landry said the incident remains under active investigation. Burnham said investigators were examining an apparent loss of steering, but the exact cause was not yet known.
MOM LOSES GRIP ON DAUGHTER AS PASSENGER FERRY CAPSIZES WITH 20 PEOPLE STILL MISSING
A map shows the site of the tanker collision at the Port of New Orleans. (Google Maps)
The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) initially announced that it was dispatching a Go Team to investigate the collision, with investigators expected to arrive on Saturday morning.
However, the agency later said that lingering flight disruptions from Friday's nationwide FAA ground stop had forced a change in plans.

"Due to the residual delays from the nationwide ground stop, the NTSB will no longer send a board member and will instead send a team of investigators by ground to the scene of the vessel collision in New Orleans," the agency wrote on X.
11-NIGHT CARIBBEAN CRUISE ABRUPTLY CANCELED AFTER COAST GUARD DETAINS SHIP

The Atlantic Asphalt tanker struck American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage around 12:30 p.m. on the Mississippi River, the Port of New Orleans said in a statement shared with Fox News. Port officials initially reported about 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, aboard. Moreno later estimated roughly 180 to 190 people were on the ship.

University Medical Center New Orleans and other LCMC Health hospitals had earlier received an estimated two dozen patients following the incident, LCMC Health said in a statement. Medical teams were evaluating patients and providing care while coordinating with emergency responders. Moreno subsequently announced the updated total of 32 hospitalized passengers.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the Coast Guard was supporting state and local responders near mile marker 96 on the Mississippi River.

"We are throwing every asset we have to help rescue missing passengers," Mullin wrote on X, adding that DHS was coordinating closely with Louisiana officials. "Our prayers are with all those impacted by this terrible tragedy."
TWO DEAD, INCLUDING INFANT, AFTER BOAT CAPSIZES IN NEW YORK HARBOR; 12 RESCUED

American Cruise Lines confirmed that guests and crew were evacuated. In an updated statement, the company thanked the Coast Guard, its crew and local first responders for their rescue efforts and said it was helping everyone aboard find accommodations.

"We are getting everyone who was aboard the ship settled into hotels and making sure they have everything they need," the company said. "We are also in close contact with the U.S. Coast Guard, New Orleans Police, and other agencies, and will continue to coordinate with them."
The United Cajun Navy said on X that it was on standby at the port.
The New Orleans Fire Department and NOLA Ready said in an earlier Facebook update that multiple people had been rescued and search and rescue operations were ongoing at the time of the post.

Acadian Ambulance said in an earlier update on X that it had transported eight patients and had 15 units and two sprint trucks on scene to assist New Orleans EMS and other first responders. The ambulance service said it was prepared to send additional units if needed.

Port NOLA Harbor Police, the New Orleans Fire Department, the New Orleans Police Department, the U.S. Coast Guard and emergency medical personnel were on scene conducting rescue and response operations.
AT LEAST 40 RESCUED, 2 DEAD AS BOAT CAPSIZES AFTER MACHETE FIGHT NEAR PUERTO RICO

Passengers were brought inside the Port of New Orleans Administration Building for triage and assistance, officials said. Moreno said crews conducted roll calls and checked hospital lists to account for everyone.

New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno, center, stands beside Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry during a news conference about the American Heritage river cruiser’s capsizing on Nov. 13, 2026. (Kat Ramirez/Fox News Digital )

Officials were arranging hotel rooms, transportation, replacement prescriptions and ways for passengers to contact relatives after losing phones, identification and other belongings. The Red Cross and medical partners were helping, Moreno said. She said no children were aboard, and no injuries were reported on the tanker.
The American Heritage had been docked about two hours before the collision to begin letting passengers off.

According to a news release, skies were clear with no precipitation around the time of the collision, with temperatures in the upper 60s and north winds of 8 to 12 mph, gusting to 15 to 17 mph. The release listed the current water temperature at around 66 degrees.

At the news conference, Landry said Moreno called him in Baton Rouge to request resources. He contacted Mullin before President Donald Trump called to offer whatever assistance Louisiana needed. Landry said the state would continue helping until passengers were able to return home.
In a follow-up post on X, Landry credited first responders with saving "countless lives" and reiterated that all passengers had been accounted for.
"Because of the heroic work of our first responders ALL PASSENGERS have been accounted for. This is nothing short of a miracle," he wrote.
Trump also praised the rescue effort in a statement shared by the White House on X.

"Thank you to the United States Coast Guard for doing such an incredible job of rescue, and other work, having to do with the crash of the two ships in Louisiana," Trump said. "Likewise, all of Law Enforcement and First Responders were fantastic."

House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., said on X that the NTSB chair called to brief him on the collision. In a post describing rescues as ongoing, before officials announced everyone was accounted for, Johnson said he was monitoring the situation and praying for passengers and crew to be recovered safely.
"So grateful for this update," Johnson wrote in a follow-up post, quoting Landry’s announcement that all passengers had been accounted for and calling the rescue "nothing short of a miracle."
Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., also thanked first responders.

"Becky and I are praying for everyone involved in the terrible ship collision in New Orleans," Kennedy wrote on X. "We’re grateful for the brave first responders working to rescue those in danger and praying everyone makes it home safely."
Rep. Troy Carter, D-La., said he was closely monitoring the response.

"I am devastated to hear about the ships crashing near the Port of New Orleans," Carter wrote on X. "I am monitoring the situation closely and praying for the swift rescue of survivors and for all emergency crews responding to the situation."
Rep. Julia Letlow, R-La., also offered prayers for passengers and first responders.

title: Animal rights activist attacks NYC horse carriage driver with skateboard during tirade, union says
summary: Abigail Holbrook allegedly punched two Central Park horse carriage drivers and struck one with a skateboard after screaming about animal abuse.
story: Abigail Holbrook, 27, is facing charges after police confirmed to Fox News Digital she used her skateboard to assault a horse carriage driver in New York City's Central Park. The Transport Workers Union is condemning the alleged attack.

An angry animal rights activist armed with a skateboard allegedly assaulted two horse-drawn carriage drivers in Central Park on Tuesday after launching an expletive-laden tirade in front of visiting families, union representatives said.
Abigail Holbrook, 27, of Philadelphia, was arrested after screaming at drivers and accusing them of "animal abuse" near a carriage stand, according to police and video of the incident.

"You’re animal abusers! Horses do not do well in New York City. They are very sensitive to light and noise," Holbrook shouted, according to video of the confrontation. "The people that are f------ using these horses are animal abusers. I’m Squid the Kid, bro. Y’all will know my f------ name."
MAMDANI ACCUSED OF BETRAYING NYC WORKERS AS UNION BOSS BLASTS 'ANTI-LABOR' HORSE CARRIAGE BAN
Abigail Holbrook, 27, is facing charges after police say she assaulted horse carriage drivers in NYC's Central Park. (Ali Yildirim)
During the altercation, Holbrook punched two 45-year-old drivers and struck one of them in the head with her skateboard, the Transport Workers Union of America (TWU) told Fox News Digital.
Both victims suffered minor injuries and declined medical treatment at the scene. Holbrook was taken into custody by the New York City Police Department and is charged with two counts of assault.
VIGIL PLANNED FOR 18-YEAR-OLD TOURIST KILLED IN CENTRAL PARK HORSE-DRAWN CARRIAGE INCIDENT
Holbrook allegedly hit the victim with her skateboard during the violent incident. (Ali Yildirim)

"This is outrageous and unacceptable," TWU Local 100 Administrative Vice President Alexander Kemp said in a statement. "We need a more visible police presence for our members at horse-carriage stands in the park to protect against these wackos. This is their place of work and people are coming just to harass and attack them. All workers deserve to be safe at work."
Christina Hansen, a union shop steward who witnessed the assault and alerted police, placed the blame on rhetoric from city leadership and advocacy groups.
MAN KILLED AFTER HORSE-DRAWN CARRIAGE BOLTS AND FLIPS NEAR POPULAR NEW YORK CITY TOURIST DESTINATION

"The problem is that a lot of people, you know, don't know anything about horses, and they get misled by these animal rights groups who liken it to slavery, and say that the horses are being tortured by being forced to drag heavy carriages around as if carriages don't have wheels," Hansen told Fox News Digital.
Hansen noted that the financial livelihoods of carriage drivers depend on whether their horses are well taken care of.

"Let's face it, these organizations ... make money by getting donations and there's no money to be made by telling people that our horses are well taken care of," she said. "I only make money if my horse is well taken care of because I can't go to work if he can't pull the carriage, if he doesn't enjoy his job ... so my monetary interest is that my horse is taken care of. Their monetary interest is that the horses are being abused or exploited or whatever."
The violence erupted amid ongoing legal and political battles surrounding the city's historic carriage industry.
CLASH IN THE CASTLE: MEDIEVAL TIMES DINNER THEATER INSIDERS ALLEGE ANIMAL CRUELTY, SEXUAL HARASSMENT
Last month, the city council voted 40 to 7 to pass Romanch's Law, named in memory of 18-year-old Romanch Mahajan, who died in June after being thrown from a runaway carriage in Central Park.
The legislation would phase out horse-drawn carriages entirely by June 1, 2028, while directing the city to establish a transition program for more than 150 drivers and industry workers.
In a statement to Fox News Digital, People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) pushed back against the union's accusations.
Horse-drawn carriages offer trips through through Central Park, Wednesday, Oct. 14, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Yuki Iwamura)
"If the horse-drawn carriage trade is suddenly concerned about hostility and violence, it might start by looking in the mirror," the group said.

Horse-drawn carriages have been a staple of Central Park and Fifth Avenue for generations, providing iconic rides for tourists visiting the city.

"Carriage horses have been pulling carriages in Central Park since the day the park opened in December 1858," said Hansen. "They've been living on Manhattan since 1625. The city would not be the city that it is, and Central Park would not be the park that it is, except for horses."

story: The driver whose pickup truck plowed into a youth soccer field and killed two and wounded ten others will not face any charges prosecutors announced. The incident that occurred on Oct. 17.

On Thursday, a 28-page report released by Sedgwick County District Attorney Marc Bennett said investigators did not find enough evidence to charge the driver, concluding the crash was the result of "negligence" rather than a criminal act.

title: SEE IT: Door-kicking pranksters target California homes as police warn trend can end badly
summary: Irvine Police Department shared surveillance videos of the door kick challenge, warning the viral prank is vandalism that can lead to criminal charges.
story: Irvine police released video showing people kicking front doors as hard as they can before running away, warning the social media challenge can damage property and lead to dangerous encounters.

A viral social media challenge that sends people running up to strangers' homes and kicking their front doors is making the rounds again, prompting California police to warn the stunt can lead to more than property damage.

The Irvine Police Department released surveillance videos on social media showing people taking part in the "Door Kick Challenge," which involves kicking someone's front door as hard as possible, recording it and running away before anyone answers.
"This isn't a prank. It's vandalism, and it can end badly," the department said.
TWO TEENS ARRESTED AFTER CARRYING WHAT LOOKED LIKE RIFLES TO DELAWARE HOMES IN LATE-NIGHT PRANK: POLICE

The videos show groups approaching homes before running away. In one clip, a group of boys gathers outside a front door as one repeatedly knocks. As they run away, one of the boys turns and kicks the door.

The department warned that the challenge could leave behind damaged property and frightened homeowners while creating the risk of a dangerous confrontation.

"A damaged door, a scared homeowner, a dangerous confrontation, criminal charges or someone getting seriously hurt can all be part of the outcome," the department said.

Irvine police have received more than 20 calls related to the Door Kick Challenge since October, including reports from residents whose homes were targeted and witnesses who saw it happen, Officer Ziggy Azarcon told Fox News Digital.
Seven incidents have resulted in vandalism reports, and the department's Youth Services Unit is investigating them.
"We have seen an increase in this last month, even though this has been an ongoing trend for the last couple of years," Azarcon said.
Police are urging parents to talk to their children about the dangers of taking part.

The warning comes less than a week after a similar door-knocking prank ended in gunfire in Boise, Idaho.

A group of boys had been playing "ding-dong ditch" at a home Nov. 7 when they returned to the property and the resident chased them and opened fire, Boise police said. title: New York City building collapse probe raises questions about neighboring property owner’s violation history
summary: N Tech Design of America defied a New York City stop-work order months before the deadly Brooklyn building collapse that killed eight people.
story: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said at an on-site news conference Thursday that an investigation is underway after a three-story building collapse on Flatbush Avenue left eight people dead. The Department of Buildings is launching sweeps of related construction sites,

The owner of a property next to the site of Wednesday’s deadly building collapse in New York City is facing scrutiny over past construction violations, including a contractor’s decision to defy a city stop-work order in March, according to public records.

Wednesday afternoon's collapse of a three-story building at 1321 Flatbush Ave. in Brooklyn resulted in the deaths of at least eight people and triggered a massive emergency response. The building collapse has raised questions about construction activity next door, where city records show prior violations and a stop-work order that was issued months beforehand.
A stop-work order was issued at the adjacent property, 2621 Bedford Ave., in March by New York City's Department of Buildings, according to public records obtained by Fox News Digital.

The agency determined that the contractors, N Tech Design of America, had failed to install proper safety precautions, which included netting and sheds, Department of Buildings spokesperson Andrew Rudansky told The Gothamist.
NYC BUILDING COLLAPSE: EIGHT BODIES RECOVERED AS FIRST RESPONDERS SEARCH FOR SURVIVORS
First responders work the scene after a building collapsed in the Brooklyn borough of New York, Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026. (AP Photo/Ryan Murphy)
One month later, an inspector with the Department of Buildings found that the demolition work had proceeded and issued a $10,000 penalty. The order was lifted on May 8.
NYC Buildings Commissioner Ahmed Tigani said during a news conference on Wednesday that excavation work was ongoing at the Bedford Avenue site when the building collapsed.

"The type of work they were conducting was excavation work on that job site. And so, that was what they were working on today. They have a plan approved for a three-story building, but they have current plans looking for a nine-story building, which has not yet been approved for. At this point, all we have at this time is excavation work in that section of the construction site," Tigani said.
Tigani said the construction workers were "digging down."
First responders work the scene after a building collapsed in the Brooklyn borough of New York, Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026. (AP Photo/Ryan Murphy)
Agency records show the Bedford Avenue building's owner, Robert Fischman, sent a letter to landlords neighboring the property in June to inform them of the excavation.
A representative for N Tech Design of America told WABC that the company performed the demolition but left the site by late April or early May, months before Wednesday's collapse.
Read the notice of construction:

Engineering plans for the neighboring construction site also addressed the potential for accumulated water to damage nearby foundations. A drainage note states that construction operations accounted for preventing water accumulation, which "could cause damage to nearby building foundations on the subject property or on adjacent properties."
It was not immediately clear whether the precautions outlined in the engineering plans had been implemented or whether any structural concerns were documented before the collapse.

"We have immediately launched a full investigation into how exactly this happened with our law enforcement partners, and we will be looking into all aspects of the building and the neighboring construction site," Tigani said.
First responders tend to a collapsed building in Brooklyn on Nov. 11, 2026. (kena betancur/AFP via Getty Images)

The New York Police Department said the first 911 call on the building collapse at 1321 Flatbush Ave. came in at 4:01 p.m. The property, a three-story mixed-use building, collapsed into an excavation pit at a neighboring construction site. The collapse also tore away a wall of 1323 Flatbush Ave., leaving apartments and stairwells exposed.

Firefighters with the New York City Fire Department reached the scene within a minute after the building collapsed, as there were already some in the area. The building contained a store at street level and apartments above it.

title: MICHAEL RUIZ: JonBenet Ramsey investigators are retesting evidence with newer technology, police chief says
summary: Boulder investigators are retesting decades-old DNA evidence in the JonBenet Ramsey cold case using advanced technology that didn't exist in 1997.
story: Boulder Police Chief Steve Redfearn and District Attorney Michael Dougherty say old evidence is being retested with state-of-the-art technology as JonBenet Ramsey's unsolved murder nears the 30-year mark.
Investigators in Boulder are retesting decades-old evidence in the murder of JonBenet Ramsey as her family nears 30 years since the unsolved slaying in their former Colorado home.

"Chief [Steve] Redfearn and I are more hopeful now than we have been in the past because of the advances in the investigation and the advances in technology," Boulder County District Attorney Michael Dougherty told reporters in a news briefing this week. "And I say that based on just how DNA has progressed over time."

Her father, John Ramsey, had spent years begging authorities to attempt to solve the case through investigative genetic genealogy, a relatively new technique for ginning up DNA leads that involves combining genetic testing results with genealogy research to identify potential persons of interest. IGG itself is rapidly evolving as state-of-the-art DNA testing also improves.
And her brother, John Andrew Ramsey, told Fox News Digital he believes the samples in police possession do contain the DNA of JonBenet's killer.
JONBENET RAMSEY'S FATHER ASKS TRUMP FOR HELP IN DAUGHTER'S UNSOLVED MURDER CASE

JonBenet Patricia Ramsey, 4, lies on a white seamless backdrop wearing white lace gloves during a studio session for a commercial ad and actress portfolio in Boulder, Colo., on May 1, 1994. (ZUMAPRESS.com)

"The testing available in the late 1990s was far less sensitive than today’s, yet it still detected this male DNA in the same spot as her blood," he said. "In 2008, touch DNA testing found the same unknown male’s DNA on both the left and right sides of the waistband of her long johns. It is the killer’s DNA."

A cold case review panel was convened in Boulder as local police, state and federal investigators continue to dig into what happened on Dec. 26, 1996, when JonBenet was found strangled and with head trauma in the basement of her home. Although investigators have pursued a number of potential suspects, persons of interest and theories about how she died over the years, no one has been convicted, and her death remains one of America's most prominent unsolved cases.

"It's no secret," Boulder Police Chief Steve Redfearn told reporters in a sit-down interview earlier this week. "We're also going back, based on that cold case review, and retesting things that were tested 30 years ago with newer technology."
MICHAEL RUIZ: JONBENÉT RAMSEY'S FATHER CHALLENGES DA AFTER REPORT SAYS FAMILY SHOULDN'T HAVE BEEN CLEARED

Boulder Police Chief Steve Redfearn and District Attorney Michael Dougherty speak with reporters at a news briefing on the JonBenet Ramsey case in November 2026. The Colorado 6-year-old's 1996 murder remains unsolved. (City of Boulder)
Redfearn appeared to confirm a recent revelation John Andrew Ramsey, who told Fox News Digital previously that the family had learned this year that new testing had begun in the fall of 2025.

"Maybe something comes of that," Redfearn said. "Not that it was missed, but maybe the technology just improved enough that we look at, hey, this item was tested in '97, we're testing it again, and hey, look, we found something that was missed in '97."
Dougherty gave an example of a recent trial that he said involved the testimony of four different DNA experts because testing had been done on multiple occasions as the technology improved.
Among the benefits of rapidly improving technology is an increasingly successful ability to identify DNA profiles contained in mixed samples, Dougherty added.
"To me, it's quantity, quality, and location of the DNA," he said.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X
Traditionally, testing a sample left behind by a single donor is straightforward, he explained.

"When it's a single source in DNA, just generally speaking, it's much easier assuming you have enough to test, particularly if it's blood or semen," he said. "But if it's touch, and it's a single source, that's different than if it's touch or saliva, and it is a mixture."

JonBenet Ramsey pictured in an undated portrait. The 6-year-old was found dead in her home on Dec. 26, 1996, in one of America's most high-profile unsolved cases. (Splash News)
When two or more people leave DNA on the same surface, it must first be untangled in a lab.

The process can be destructive to the evidence, especially when there isn't much left, he said, and that complicates things under evidence rules that must be validated and stand up in court.
SEND US A TIP

"We're not gonna do it recklessly, to use Chief Redfearn's word," Dougherty said. "We're also not gonna hesitate. We recognize the clock's ticking. None of us are gonna be here forever. We wanna see this case solved for everyone involved and everyone impacted by it. And we're absolutely committed to doing that."

John Ramsey speaks with Fox News Digital in Las Vegas in April 2022. He is the father of JonBenet Ramsey, the 6-year-old whose murder on Dec. 26, 1996, remains unsolved nearly 30 years later. (Michael Ruiz/Fox News Digital)
John Andrew Ramsey questioned how much of the sample is available for testing by investigators now and whether there's enough to be re-tested by a potential criminal defense team in the future.
"Do we really only have one shot at this?" he asked.
JONBENET RAMSEY CASE: FATHER REMEMBERS 'DADDY'S GIRL' ON WHAT WOULD BE HER 32ND BIRTHDAY

Separately, Redfearn told reporters that if the new DNA testing fails to yield results, investigators have additional previously unreleased evidence they could make public in the hope that someone comes forward.

"There’s still plenty of things that are not out there that we have," he told reporters.
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL
While tips continue to come in regularly almost three decades after JonBenet's slaying, investigators are still asking anyone who may have information to come forward.

"There is more than one someone out there that knows something," Redfearn said.

title: Couple accused of killing registered sex offender in pre-planned stabbing in Arizona desert
summary: A couple allegedly planned the stabbing of a registered sex offender in a desert area in Arizona and now face first-degree homicide charges, police say.
story: An Arizona couple faces first-degree homicide charges after police said they planned and carried out the stabbing death of a registered sex offender, then left his body in a remote desert area.
An Arizona couple was arrested after allegedly stabbing a registered sex offender to death in a desert area of the state, according to authorities.

Jacob Middlebrook, 35, and his girlfriend, Layne McIntosh, 36, were initially taken into custody for second-degree homicide in the death of 29-year-old Arron Christopher Warren, Bullhead City Police said on social media.

Police began investigating after a motorist found a dead man on the side of the road in the 3100 block of Silver Creek Road on Saturday. The circumstances surrounding the man’s death appeared suspicious, so detectives were called to the scene to conduct a homicide investigation.
MICHIGAN DECISION FORCES REMOVAL OF DISGRACED SPORTS DOCTOR LARRY NASSAR FROM SEX OFFENDER REGISTRY
Jacob Middlebrook and his girlfriend, Layne McIntosh, are facing homicide charges. (Bullhead City Police)
Detectives later identified the man as Warren, a Bullhead City "transient." Detectives also identified a possible suspect and discovered that the victim’s vehicle was missing.
Hours later, Las Vegas Metro Police assisted Bullhead City investigators and located the victim’s vehicle parked at a casino in Laughlin, Nevada.

Middlebrook and McIntosh were taken into custody by Las Vegas Metro Police and booked into the Clark County Detention Center in Las Vegas, where they will be held until they can be extradited to Mohave County, Arizona.
On Monday, the pair's charges were upgraded to first-degree homicide.
CALIFORNIA SHERIFF FIGHTS PLAN TO HOUSE CONVICTED SEX PREDATOR NEAR GIRL SCOUT CAMP
Investigators determined that the two were also "local transients" who had known the victim for the past few months.
"Detectives discovered that the couple had expressed distaste for registered sex offenders and had planned the homicide in advance," Bullhead City police said.

"The couple reportedly pre-determined the desert location where they intended to leave Warren’s body. They also reportedly measured furniture/beds that could be large enough to cover the victim’s body along the side of the road. Warren was a registered Level 2 sex offender," the post added.
Police in Bullhead City, Arizona, say a couple allegedly stabbed a registered sex offender to death and planned the homicide in advance. (Bullhead City Police)

Bullhead City Police Chief Paul George said the department updates the community when certain registered sex offenders move in or change addresses but that he "will not tolerate anyone using this information as a reason to threaten, intimidate, harass or harm another person."

"When a Level 2 or Level 3 sex offender moves into our area or, more commonly, changes addresses, the Bullhead City Police Department shares that information as a public service to help keep residents informed," he said in a statement. "While required notifications are mailed to residents living within an approximate 1,000 feet radius of an offender’s registered address, we go a step further by sharing these notifications on social media to reach a broader audience. Our goal is to provide information, not create fear or alarm. We believe an informed community is a safer community."

"Our Bureau of Criminal Investigations conducts monthly address verification checks to help ensure registered sex offenders are complying with registration requirements. Our responsibility is to protect our community, keep residents informed and to enforce the law. We take all three of these seriously," George continued.

title: DHS touts highest ICE deportations in history, as Mullin says agency has been ‘unleashed’
summary: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin announced record ICE arrests and deportations in fiscal 2026, with arrests exceeding three Biden fiscal years combined.
story: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin discusses the future of the Trump administration’s immigration policy and the viability of working with Democrats on ‘The Ingraham Angle.’

Immigration officials on Thursday announced a historic milestone, saying arrests and deportations this year reached the highest levels in the agency’s history, with arrests surpassing the combined totals of the Biden administration’s final three years and deportations nearly matching them.
"Fiscal year 2026 saw the highest number of ICE deportations and arrests for any year in ICE’s history," Secretary Markwayne Mullin, Department of Homeland Security (DHS), said.

"The total number of ICE arrests in Fiscal Year 2026 was more than all three full fiscal years under Biden combined, as the patriots of ICE work around the clock to make America safe again. Thanks to President Trump’s leadership, ICE has been unleashed to target and remove illegal aliens so that we can save American lives."
Officials made more than 491,000 arrests, including nearly 475,000 administrative arrests, the highest administrative total in agency history.
MULLIN VOWS ‘ZERO CHANGE’ ON IMMIGRATION AFTER REPUBLICANS SUFFER CRUSHING MIDTERM LOSSES
DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin credited Trump’s leadership for record ICE arrests and deportations, saying the agency has been "unleashed." (Cliff Owen)
ICE also carried out 483,200 deportations this fiscal year, surpassing the previous agency record of 442,640 set the year before.
Total arrests exceeded the combined figures for fiscal years 2022, 2023 and 2024 under the Biden administration by nearly 65,000, DHS said.
Meanwhile, deportations this fiscal year nearly matched the combined total for all three full fiscal years under Biden, falling short by fewer than 3,000, according to the department.
WHITE HOUSE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER TRUMP ANGERS BASE BY FLOATING ILLEGAL ALIEN DEAL WITH DEMS
Trump’s immigration crackdown drove ICE arrests and deportations to historic highs in fiscal 2026, according to DHS. (Christian Torres/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images)
Specifically, this year's arrests were more than six times higher than those recorded during former President Joe Biden's first fiscal year in office.
Deportations were also more than eight times higher for the same time period.
August 2026 also set a new record for arrests, with 50,925, marking the highest number for any single month in ICE history, Mullin said.
That pace continued into September, which logged over 48,000 arrests, representing a more than 300% increase over the average September under the previous administration.

ICE deported 483,200 people in fiscal 2026, nearly matching the combined total from Biden’s final three full fiscal years, DHS said. (REUTERS/Carielle Doe)
Under Trump's leadership, more than 3 million migrants have left the U.S., DHS said.
As of October, the administration had deported nearly 1.2 million illegal aliens and arrested more than 1.25 million, according to the department.
"I couldn’t be prouder of the brave men and women of ICE, who just broke more historic records," Mullin said.

title: Texas man executed for beheading 3 children: 'Going to be with my kids'
summary: John Allen Rubio thanked loved ones and said he would soon be with the three children he killed before receiving a lethal injection in Texas.
story: Three states carried out executions on the same day, while California Gov. Gavin Newsom announced plans to commute all 548 of his state’s death sentences.
A South Texas man convicted of murdering three young children he helped raise was executed Thursday evening, nearly 23 years after the killings.
John Allen Rubio, 46, of Brownsville, received a lethal injection at a state prison in Huntsville, according to The Associated Press (AP).

Rubio was convicted of stabbing and beheading his children, Julissa Quezada, 3, John Esteban Rubio, 1, and Mary Jane Rubio, 2 months old. He was prosecuted alongside his common-law wife, Angela Camacho.
Rubio was pronounced dead at 6:47 p.m., 21 minutes after the lethal injection began, The AP said.
OKLAHOMA MAN, 73, EXECUTED FOR PLOTTING MURDER OF LOVER'S HUSBAND, OFFERS NO LAST WORDS

A fence, barbed wire and a guard are visible at a Texas prison on Jan. 22, 2025. John Allen Rubio was executed in Texas Nov. 12, 2026.  (Cecile Clocheret/AFP via Getty Images; Texas Department of Criminal Justice via AP)
The execution, scheduled for 6 p.m., proceeded without incident.

In his final statement, Rubio thanked his friends and family for their "love and understanding," acknowledged that he was "not the same person I once was" and expressed his love for his wife, according to the AP.
"I want to say I’m sorry to my wife’s family," he said. "I can’t change the past, but I can tell you my life is going to be over. But that’s not going to make you happy.
"I’m going to be with my kids in a little bit," he added. "I’m ready to go to heaven to be with my lord and savior."
ALABAMA GOVERNOR COMMUTES DEATH SENTENCE AS DOUBTS EMERGE ABOUT EVIDENCE IN MURDER CONVICTION
John Allen Rubio was convicted of murdering three young children in 2003 and sentenced to death. (Texas Department of Criminal Justice )
The execution brought an end to a case dating back to March 11, 2003, when Rubio and Camacho killed their three children inside a windowless apartment.
According to court records, Rubio was not the biological father of the two older children but had nevertheless taken on a parental role in their lives, the outlet reported.
In the lead-up to the killings, Rubio reportedly claimed the children were possessed and cast himself as the "chosen one" destined to save the world.
Rubio at one point pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity. Defense experts reportedly diagnosed him with paranoid schizophrenia, but prosecution experts ultimately disputed the findings.
His defense team also painted a picture of a deeply troubled childhood, citing violence, toxic parents, drug use and prostitution as factors that stunted his development, the AP said.
Camacho pleaded guilty and is serving a life sentence for her role in the murders, according to reports.
The apartment building where the children were killed has since been demolished, and the property was transformed into a community park and garden, according to the AP.

This photo provided by the Oklahoma Department of Corrections shows James Pavatt in February 2023. Pavatt was executed just hours before Rubio was administered lethal injection.  (Bryan Terry/The Oklahoman/USA Today Network; Oklahoma Department of Corrections via AP)

Rubio's death marked the second of two executions scheduled in the U.S. for Thursday.
Just hours earlier, James Pavatt, 73, was put to death by lethal injection in Oklahoma. Pavatt was convicted of plotting and carrying out the 2001 killing of his partner's estranged husband.

She and her husband of four years, Mark Longo, were planning to attend a TikTok event when officers approached them, according to the New York Post.

Longo said his wife's detention stemmed from what he described as a minor paperwork issue, The AP said. The couple reportedly made an error on one of her immigration forms and failed to catch it while dealing with the seizure and euthanasia of Peanut.

PEANUT THE PET SQUIRREL TAKEN AWAY BY NEW YORK STATE OFFICIALS FROM ADOPTED HOME, MAY BE EUTHANIZED
